pool.text: European settlers arrived in the area, led by a British mining engineer named Albert Kitson.
The first shipment of coal was made to Britain under Colonial Governor Frederick Lugard.
The city acquired township status and was called Enugwu-Ngwo.
The city was renamed Enugu due to rapid expansion towards other indigenous communities.
Enugu became an anti-colonial symbol after the tragic massacre of striking coal miners.
The area became part of the post-independence Eastern Region after independence.
The Catholic Diocese of Enugu was established with suffragan dioceses of Onitsha.
The city of Enugu was named the Biafran capital until federal forces captured it.
Anambra State including Enugu was formed by the regime of Murtala Muhammed.
The Catholic diocese of Nsukka was established with parishes under Bishop Godfrey Igwebuike Onah.
Part of Enugu State's east was removed to form a part of Ebonyi State.
The Catholic diocese of Awgu was established with 48 parishes under Bishop John Ifeanyichukwu Okoye.
Chime was elected by the people of Enugu State and sworn into office.
Enugu reached an estimated population of over 4.4 million residents.
A new leader was elected by the people and sworn into office in May.
A new partnership was established between the state government and China's Haier Group.
